headline: As in task_094, the documents disagree on whether the Gold Rewards Card's 0.025% stacks, so the correct credit could be $98 or $100.

issues.summary: Gold expects 6.85% (5.5 + 0.75 Green + 0.6 EcoCard), treating the Gold Rewards Card 0.025% as a credit-card bonus outranked by the EcoCard. doc_013, a required doc, describes it as a separate relationship bonus that stacks, which gives 6.875% and a $100.00 credit.
evidence: doc_savings_accounts_gold_account_013: "As a Gold Rewards Card holder, you receive an additional 0.025% relationship bonus APY on top of the base rate." and the example "Total APY with the bonus: 6.0%" (5.5 + 0.025 is 5.525)

doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_045: "credit card APY bonuses DO stack with other types of bonuses, such as: ... Relationship bonuses for holding multiple Rho-Bank products"; its example lists "Gold Rewards Card: +0.025% APY bonus" among non-stacking card bonuses
db credit_card_accounts: cc_lm83h7k2p5_gold "Gold Rewards Card", cc_lm83h7k2p5_eco "EcoCard", cc_lm83h7k2p5_platinum
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that adds the doc_013 relationship bonus credits $100.00 and fails. The actual 5.625% also decomposes either as base+Purple+GR-card bonus or as base+Purple+relationship bonus, which does not settle the question.
issues.suggested_fix: Make doc_013 and doc_014 non-overlapping (declare the 0.025% a card bonus subject to highest-only stacking) and fix doc_013's "6.0%" example.

solution_check: Base 5.5%. Checking boosts Green +0.75% vs Purple +0.1% (purple_001); highest only (doc_046) gives 0.75. Card bonuses Platinum 0.15, Gold Rewards 0.025, EcoCard 0.6; highest gives 0.6. Expected 6.85%. Actual = 450 x 12 / 96000 = 5.625%. Credit $98.00, matching gold[6] under the card-bonus reading.
prior_note: The prior Major (doc_013 vs doc_014 bonus ambiguity) persists unchanged in v1.0.1; only the credit amount is graded, since the report table does not exist.
notes: submit_interest_discrepancy_report_7294 calls add_to_db("interest_discrepancy_reports", ...), but TransactionalDB has no such table, so add_to_db returns False and the tool still prints success. The report persists nothing; only its tool name in agent_discoverable_tools (a write, always logged) is graded. Its expected_apy, actual_apy, and amount_difference arguments therefore never affect the DB result; only the apply_savings_account_credit_6831 amount does (it changes accounts.current_holdings and a transaction_id hashed from the amount). The savings docs say interest is "compounded daily" from a daily periodic rate, but every posted credit equals balance x APY / 12 exactly. Gold uses that monthly convention, and an agent that back-solves actual_apy from the posted credit adopts it naturally. A literal daily-compounding computation would give a slightly different credit. Customer misnames the Silver Rewards Card and the script self-corrects; the DB shows the Gold Rewards Card, so there is no impact.
